title: a-refused-ask-leaves-a-row
intention: An ask that RAISES inside resolver() lands a row in inference_domain's ask record, naming the refusal, so the refusal rate of this system's only inference door is readable by the same read that counts answers. Today the store is an ANSWER record wearing an ask record's name.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 at cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, resolve(): the inference_calls row is written only AFTER `result = resolver(request)` returns. A raise means no write. The corpus stands at 2520 rows — 1386 miss, 1134 hit — and zero rows for any ask that failed.

FOUND BY TRYING TO BUILD A WATCH ON IT. Ticket a-non-final-answer-is-refused-by-name specified its WATCHME as 'the probe reads the domain's own ask log' to count refusals; the log cannot count them, so the probe had to be written around the absence — it watches the fault RETURNING (a cached contentless zero-cost row) instead of the guard firing. That is an honest watch and a weaker one, and the reason it is weaker is this defect.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is not hypothetical: the voyage before that one explained a failed drive with a cause it had not measured, and the false sentence went into an append-only history, a ticket distinction and a slate. Four real refusals were produced against a cold hex in one sitting the next day; not one of them is countable today. When a failure leaves no row, the only record of it is whatever a human wrote down about it — and a human wrote it down wrong. This is Law 3 at the door: the refusal rate is not measured, so it is not known, and the space where a number should be gets filled with narration.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the refusal rate of the only inference door is unmeasured, so it is unknown, and narration fills the gap), Law 7 (errors are permanent in records of truth; an error that leaves no record at all is the limit case), Law 10 (nothing in the system is immeasurable — 'we have not built the measurement yet' is the true and ordinary state this ticket ends).

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs the proofs beside cairn/devices/inference_domain/ under isolation=netns, with at least one tooth that is RED on unmodified HEAD for the right reason — a resolver stubbed to raise, asserted to leave a row, which today leaves none. NON-HOLLOW CLAUSE: a tooth that merely asserts 'resolve raises' is green on HEAD and proves nothing; the tooth must read the STORE back after the raise. LIVE GATE: one real cold-hex ask that raises HostNonFinal, then the row read back out of inference_calls — the fixture world cannot show whether the real write door admits the shape. FEEDBACK EDGE: on failure the finding returns to this ticket and to inference_domain's charter, which is where clause (9) already names the refusal path.
falsifier.proves_red: FALSIFIER: DONE when an ask that raises inside resolver() lands a row in the domain's ask record naming the refusal, so the count of refusals is readable from the store by the same read that counts answers. RED on any of: (1) a raise inside resolver() leaves no row — the defect standing; (2) the row for a refused ask is indistinguishable from an answered one, so a reader counting answers silently counts refusals among them (Law 7 — a record of truth may not carry an error quietly); (3) the refusal row is served back as a CACHE HIT to a later asker of the same canonical question — a refusal is not an answer and must never be replayed as one, and getting this wrong converts a loud error into a permanent wrong answer, which is strictly worse than the defect being fixed; (4) writing the row changes what a SUCCESSFUL ask stores or costs — the fix breaking the path it was meant to complete; (5) the refusal row is written anywhere other than through db_domain's existing write door (Law 6 — the holder gates writes to its own state). HORIZON: the next cold-hex drive of the aider_shim apprentice, which is the event that reliably produces refusals, and no later than the next voyage that dials inference at all.
falsifier.horizon: the next cold-hex drive of the aider_shim apprentice — the event that reliably produces refusals — and no later than the next voyage that dials inference at all

how:
First cut. Record the row on the way OUT of resolve() whether the resolver returned or raised, so the record is written by the frame rather than by the success path — the same shape harbor_master's clearance door uses for exactly this reason (a writer at the frame cannot miss a refusal nobody has thought of yet). The refused row carries the exception type and its message, cost 0, and a marker distinguishing it from an answer.

TWO THINGS THE BUILD MUST SETTLE FIRST, both named in the cast rather than assumed: WHICH raises earn a row (BadRequest fires before anything is spent and may not deserve one), and whether the row shape passes db_domain's existing write door unchanged. Both are read off the code at build time.

AND THE THIRD FALSIFIER CLAUSE IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, not an afterthought: a refusal must never be served back as a cache HIT. Recording a failure inside a store whose purpose is replaying stored answers is where this fix could end up worse than the defect.
